summary: The four indexed w48 findings are E1: related physical-design automation papers and Nazca release documentation, with no indexed E2/E3 or usage analytics in the supplied snapshot. Existing automation and code-based inspection weaken a generic visual or agent differentiation claim; the papers do not show that Lunima saves engineering effort. Workshop-feedback summaries remain leads to direct evidence, but their original records are unavailable, as are the earlier experiment registrations and several required product-context documents. The supplied critic's objections are incorporated: park the foundry opportunity, treat public silence as unknown use, retain education without claiming adoption, and reuse installed-release findings as delivery QA. The proposal bundles existing human decisions and prepares a conditional, matched manual-code versus agent-assisted pilot; no new experiment, outreach, campaign or spending is authorized.
critic_summary: Build nothing new this week; DR-0001 correctly refuses a strategic commitment on E1 evidence, but its conditional pilot is not yet a discriminating test of agent value. All four w48 quotations and dates match the opened sources; three papers share authors and none establishes demand for Lunima. Drop the proposed expanded I:foreign-layout-and-verification update this week: the frozen interview protocol is unavailable, and a six-hypothesis task search cannot be certified as the existing scope. Retain I:returning-testers as the single existing usage inquiry, starting with already-known records and including non-returners after approval. Drop any claim of AI superiority from the proposed two-workflow comparison: it changes the toolchain and agent assistance together, while GDSFactory+ already supplies an MCP workflow. Consolidate the queue locally, recover the original protocols, and defer pilot preparation until one real task justifies its setup and validation costs.
